names.name: party wing
names.said: Said by a package, not by a person. Nobody orders party wings in a bar.

etymology.root: party + wing; retail compound, on the pattern of party pack and party size, where party means quantity-for-sharing rather than any occasion
etymology.note: No dated first use found for this project. Newspaper and trade archives were not searched to exhaustion, and the phrase is a grocery coinage, so it may well predate anything indexed. Sanderson Farms prints it as 'Chicken Party Wings Flats & Drummettes' — the label carries both the marketing word and the two trade words at once.

text.what: A supermarket's name for wings already broken down: tips off, joint cut, drumettes and flats loose in one bag or tray. The work a bar's prep cook does, done at the plant. The word says nothing about seasoning and nothing about size — it says only that you will not be cutting anything.
text.how: Thaw, pat dry, cook. The pieces come mixed in whatever ratio the case gave, roughly one drumette per flat, which is why a home cook cannot order all flats and a chain sometimes can.
text.today: Sold fresh and frozen, plain and pre-seasoned, and the count drives January. Super Bowl week is the year's peak: the National Chicken Council put the 2026 game at 1.48 billion wings.
